key_insight: Brine injection rate and pore-scale heterogeneity strongly control how trapped hydrogen is remobilized and redistributed during imbibition in sandstone.
engineering_relevance: Hydrogen storage models should account for transient trapping, capillary effects, and rock heterogeneity to better predict recovery and storage efficiency.
method: Fast in-situ synchrotron X-ray micro-CT imaging of a heterogeneous sandstone
Systematic variation of brine injection rate during imbibition
Quantification of hydrogen mobilisation, recovery, and trapped-cluster evolution
evidence_signal: The tomography data showed significant mobilisation of disconnected hydrogen clusters even at low capillary numbers below 10^-6, with heterogeneity affecting early-stage trapping.
watch_item: Results come from pore-scale imaging of a specific sandstone sample, so broader reservoir-scale behavior will still require upscaling and validation across rock types.
paper_title: Flow-rate controls on trapped hydrogen redistribution in a heterogeneous sandstone: a synchrotron X-ray micro-CT study
